title: passed.json / reject.json / held.json / review.json (schema 2.0)
description: aggregate --phase final writes the four lists into revisions/r<NNNN>/ (design doc 06, sections 1 and 3). passed, reject and held are disjoint and together cover every episode of the task except those skipped for missing source files (D40); review is an orthogonal view: mostly passed episodes waiting for a human, plus rejects that may be appealed. Identical episodes are not removed (D87): the duplicate check only reports them. A reject's reasons name every blocking finding (module, code, item), and review items name the findings they ask about (design doc 17 §4.3, §4.4). Review items (D42, the registry's review lines): task_verdict for task_success's review findings on episodes in passed without a human verdict - an episode already rejected (by any module) is not asked, held episodes get no items until resolved; reject_appeal for every reject whose blocking findings are all appealable (C1 appealable) that has no effective appeal decision and is not discarded - an 'unsure' appeal keeps it listed; eef_check for the EEF module's conflicts on episodes in passed that no person answered - an 'unsure' keeps it listed; integrity_check (design doc 14) likewise for episodes in passed the data integrity module suspects, whose rejects are final. Appeal candidates are optional and never count as pending (C1 counts_as_pending). A restore overrides only the appealed findings: an episode another module errored on goes to held until a retry succeeds. Skipped episodes are in none of the four lists; the report lists them under integrity.skipped_episodes.

reasons.description: reject: every reason - the blocking findings (with code and item), a person's discard or failure; held: which module could not judge it. Modules that failed on a rejected episode are listed with kind execution_error (D35)

appealable.description: the code may be appealed (registry 2.0, D42)

findings.description: passed / reject / held (F12.5, design doc 17 §5.4): every finding of the episode, every module, with the level it has in this revision - the task's policy after the applied human decisions: a person's conclusion is a blocking finding of its own (human), an appeal turns the appealable blocking findings to info, a settled review finding is gone. What the console lists and filters the episodes by

line.description: review: the registry line it is asked on

index.description: its position in the findings of the module's record; absent on a person's conclusion

human.description: a person's conclusion; message_zh is its text

review.description: review.json only: what a person is asked to decide - one item per review line and source module, naming the findings it asks about

kind.description: the review_kind of a registry review line (C1, D43); today task_verdict, reject_appeal, eef_consistency, integrity_suspect

line.description: the registry line id of this kind (eef_check for eef_consistency, integrity_check for integrity_suspect, otherwise the kind itself); the Daemon's adjudication line

codes.description: the review-level findings (or, for reject_appeal, the appealable blocking findings) the question is about
